{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France#Alsace|Alsatian recipes]]

'''Choucroute garnie''' is a dish of Sauerkraut with sausages, salt pork, and potatoes. Being a little picky about your ingredients (especially the sauerkraut) with this recipe makes all the difference.

==Ingredients==
*1 or so [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] of [[Cookbook:Duck|duck]] [[Cookbook:Fat|fat]]
*1 medium [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*2–3 small [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]]
*5 [[Cookbook:Juniper Berry|juniper berries]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Clove|clove]]
*1–2 [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] cloves
*1 or so tablespoons of [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander seed]]
*½ tablespoon [[Cookbook:Mustard|black mustard seed]]
*2 strips of [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]] (or the same amount of salted [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] belly), sliced into rough squares
*1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] of [[Cookbook:Sauerkraut|sauerkraut]]
*4 pork [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausages]]
*3 smoked pork slices, bone in
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) or so of [[Cookbook:White Wine|white wine]] (dry)

==Procedure==
#In a [[Cookbook:Pots and Pans|pot]] large enough to in the end hold everything, melt the duck fat over medium heat.
#When hot, add the onions and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] until translucent (about 5 minutes or so).
#Then, add the sauerkraut, white wine, juniper berries, clove, coriander seed, mustard seed, and garlic.
#Add the smoked pork and bacon.
#Cover, and then [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 2 hours.
#In other pot, simmer the peeled potatoes and your sausages—don't boil, or your sausages will split open.
#Simmer until potatoes are done (and by then the sausage will be, too).
#Serve in a heap—sauerkraut at the bottom, various [[Cookbook:Pork|pig]] and potato parts on top.
